mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in the month preceding the forecast date reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected equity cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in the preceding month
regime_hint: Rising inflationary bias in the Fed’s policy framework
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from the 30-day prior period (t-test p > 0.1), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 5.25% in the preceding month.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +2% in a month, it signals accelerating inflation expectations that prompt the market to discount future equities more aggressively, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: Early-stage inflation acceleration detected in core price pressures
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in >70% of similar inflation spikes (rolling window), or the 12-mo CPIAUCSL change is ≤ +2% in all observed spikes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS of at least 5,000 above the prior month's level indicates strengthening labor market conditions, which raises consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: Gradual labor market strengthening without wage inflation
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive in 60% of PAYEMS ≥ 5,000 monthly increases (rolling window), or unemployment falls < 3.5% in the same window.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly change in GDPC1 exceeds +4% (seasonally adjusted), it reflects robust consumer demand that supports corporate earnings growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
regime_hint: Surge in consumer durable and nondurable spending
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in >50% of GDPC1 > +4% monthly changes (rolling 12 months), or GDP growth < 2% in the same period.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO of at least 3 points signals softening supply-side constraints (e.g., manufacturing capacity), which reduces upward pricing pressure and encourages risk-on positioning, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: Early-stage easing in manufacturing capacity utilization
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive in 70% of INDPRO ≤ -3 events (rolling window), or industrial production growth > 1% in the same window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous monthly increases in HOUST (>100 units) and PAYEMS (>10,000) suggest expanding business activity and employment, reinforcing optimism about earnings prospects and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST month-on-month increase > +100 AND PAYEMS month-on-month increase > +10,000
regime_hint: Concurrent strength in both supply chain activity and labor market
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in >50% of such dual-proxy events (rolling window), or either HOUST or PAYEMS does not meet the threshold in the same window.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 6.5% for two consecutive months, it indicates a tightening labor market, prompting higher wage growth expectations and a flight to quality equities, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE month-on-month change < -0.5% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Tightening labor market reflected in falling unemployment rates
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not positive in >60% of UNRATE < 6.5% (two-month streak) events (rolling window), or unemployment rises > 6.5% in the same window.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (defined by FEDFUNDS < 1% for three consecutive months), the market anticipates future rate cuts, lowering real discount rates and supporting equity valuations, which tends to produce positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive in >80% of three-month FEDFUNDS < 1% streaks (rolling window), or FEDFUNDS ≥ 1% in all such streaks observed.
